citations.review_text: I refuse playing a platformer with no controller support. It's an immediate uninstall + refund attempt. You can't jump, you can't quit, you can select options on the controller but you can only click on them with the keyboard; it's a true nightmare of amateurism. If you go on settings and try mapping the controller yourself, it won't allow you to choose buttons. The artists behind the beautiful graphics truly deserved a competent team of developers with them. It's unprofessional and disrespectful the way it is. Not to say they lie on Steam (and to us) by saying "full controller support". (My setup is a macbook pro + xbox controller, both stated as supported by the publisher.)
This games controls ENRAGES me and is a pain in the ass to bind new ones on PS5 controller, still kick ass though

Extremely poor controller support for such a "soulslike" game that takes itself so seriously. If I connect my DualSense on Windows or Linux, I see button numbers for button prompts, and the controls are mapped all wrong. If I enable Steam Input on Linux, the controls do work. If I enable Steam Input on Windows, I get keyboard prompts. My friend to whom I actually gifted the game has reported controller input issues on macOS as well, with an Xbox Series controller. I seriously wish this game was in a playable state.

First of all, I want to talk about the art style. My god, it is probably one of the best ways that the game makes you feel bleak and hopeless. It is genuinely perfect for this game. And this is not to say that the whole game looks the same. The diversity between zones and their color pallets is immaculate, yet it still can carry this same feeling within all of them. Which is helped by the ambience and the songs of the game. These environmental factors within the game just blend in so smoothly to the point that I genuinely don't think there is a much better representation of suffering portrayed in a humane way through just the environment of any other game. Yes, Scorn also has these factors of suffering portrayed through it's environment for example, but it feels more alien while Blasphemous has this more grounded feeling to it.

Another thing I just adore is the simplicity of the games mechanics. I am aware that not being able to swing while walking is kinda aggravating, which is one of my few criticism of the mechanics, but the rest of the mechanics just feel so nice and smooth. Except one thing, parkour segments. This games parkour segments are brought straight from the core of suffering, I hate the parkour arenas with my life. This game is clearly not geared towards those parkour segments, it just feels stuffed in to an experience that's nice and slim yet still feels very fulfilling. 

The enemy designs are also so immaculate, I just cannot compliment the art direction of this game more. And the bosses are actually pretty fun. I think they have this level of attack speed that you can comprehend what they are gonna do, it's just the question of how is your positioning within the arena. And it's plenty effective, you genuinely feel like you are dancing within these fights. Except... the last boss fight (n…

So, who do I have to yell at? Why did nobody tell me how amazing this game is? I could not stop playing it. The art style is just plain beautiful; I am not even the biggest fan of pixel art, but they created something truly amazing here. The atmosphere, the despair, and the religious mania are all absolutely delectable. The bosses were bizarre, unique, and a bit horrifying at times.

The difficulty wasn’t too bad for me. Having played Nine Sols and Hollow Knight recently, I felt fully prepared for this game. I got Ending A, fighting the true final boss on normal mode. I am not going to bother with New Game+ because my backlog is just too packed to get through.

Blasphemous features a ton of exploration, but it always does so with a clear purpose. The world really pulls you in and gives you just enough to chew on to keep you asking questions. The lore can be cryptic in some areas, which only made me want to know more once the credits rolled. It is a wonderfully compact, punchy experience.

While mileage may vary, I honestly stomped most of the bosses in this game pretty hard. The very first boss kicked my ass a bit, but after that, I just blasted right ahead. I didn't think I would be giving this game a 10/10, but here we are. I ran into no major bugs—well, except for one instance where a ghost enemy got stuck inside a wall and became unkillable, forcing me to restart. Still, it was only a one-minute detour that didn’t kill the vibe.

I did have to look a few things up because I didn’t feel like running around clueless regarding how to use certain items. The church allowing you to unlock fast travel for a 20k donation was completely unexpected, but I will gladly take "save point transport for $100."Some backtracking was required, but I didn’t really mind it. Once I had everything going, I could just jump and dodge over enemies. Plus, unlocking that random movement speed wheel relic made traversing the map all the better. I actually really liked the deliberate…

I don't like this game.

The story doesn't make much sense, but that's not what I want to talk about. As a platformer souls-like, this game is punishing. In a way that [i]doesn't respect your time[/i].

Spikes and pits instantly kill you. The bosses lock you in a corner and force you to parry over and over again to survive a fight against a glorified health sponge. Platforming is clunky and unimaginative, and the mechanic of hitting an object to double-jump is terribly implemented. Most of the "magic" enemies don't make sense thematically and are extremely hard to hit - in a game where the main character is unresponsive and slow, these enemies are incredibly frustrating.

You'd think that the upgrades would help, but most of them are either gimmicks or lie about what they do. The moss in a jar SAYS it protects against poison, so you can survive in the sewer area, right? Wrong. Say goodbye to your entire fervour bar while trying to get items that could be helpful to progression. Or they might just be old body parts that some old fart seems obsessed with collecting.

It is also incredibly easy to fall through the floor.

Will I be finishing this just so I can't say I wasted 10 hours of my time? Yes. Do I think this is fun enough to ever play again or recommend to other people? no. horrible design flaws in the levels and movement, instant death spikes make for unbearable obstacles at times, getting stunlocked constantly, discoveries and upgrades are highly unintuitive, and whoever they dragged out the mud to be in charge of balancing shouldn't ever balance a game again. excited for the second one that apparently fixed a lot of these flaws

Its really sad that I cant recommend this game. Its good in what should be the main aspects (atmosphere, combat), but its horendous in what should be a side aspect (platforming).
The physics are like the 90s megaman games and trust me, there is a reason most developers dont use them. There are a lot of tight jumps you just cant say if you can make them and whether you will grab on that ledge or not. A ton of ladderhopping where you sometimes just miss the few pixels where you can grad the ladder andholding up while going through the ladder doenst work every time either. And there is a lot, and I mean a LOT of these things in the game. That paired with instant-deaths under every platforming section (i guess around 25% of all terrain might be insta-kill terrain) makes it really frustrating to move around in this game.
The levels are designed so that if you just go the way youre supposed to be, there are jumps that will kill you and it is not possible to know that beforehand. Also there are a lot of screen transitions that will 100% kill you if you just keep pressing the directional button.
This is especially hurtful in backtracking where you will definitely just fall to your death because you want to go back to a spot you where before but arent paying too much attention because the enemies are all dead and its the 5th time you walk that way. There are also special platforming challenges which are just ridiculous for really no reason. For example, you have to hit obstables in the air while pressing down und the attack button to get through a section. There is also a special attack you do by holding down and the attack button. For some reason, if you hit these obstacles in the air, the amount of time you have to hold down and the attack button to do the combo is far, far shorter than when you do it usually. This leads to a lot of times where you perform this special attack and it just plunges you to your death. Since its actually not so usefull with the full holding tim…

I played Blasphemous 2 before playing this and now I can't recommend this game. The second game is better in nearly every aspect. Better controls, levels, QOL upgrades, menus, map, bosses, platforming.

If I had to fix a few things in this game to greatly improve the experience they would be:
1. Pogo'ing is poorly implemented and hard to execute in basic conditions (also, the game never tells you that you can do it)
2. Progressing the story toward the end gets difficult, as in, you don't know what to do next. You will also end up with many quest items that take complex knowledge to know where they go.
3. Ladders. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. If you are off center by a millimeter on a ladder you will just plummet to your death.
4. Leaving rooms and re-entering to get items. I can guarantee this was a software architecture mistake. Many items you get require you to leave a room and come back immediately, and they are just on the floor. They didn't code it to drop items while you were present.

Overall the game was fine, decent even. But the things I listed above and the fact that they are fixed in number 2 ruins this game.

I understand making a game "retro" but there's no reason to ignore what makes games better now.

Movement is clunky and input lag makes fighting feel like a slog.

Enemy placement is like the original Castlevania, intenionally a** to pad gametime by making traversing unnecessarily hard. 

Hitboxes are inconsistent. 
There's no telegraphing of what enemies you can safely dash through and which will dmg you for trying. 
Parry is a thing that exists but it's completely random what enemies can actually be parried and which ones will push you back into the next abyss. 
Right at the start there's 2 types that use one-handed shortswords, one can be parried, the other pushes you back. 
Which makes the choice to make the first area right after Tutorial a Mountain with changing winds (pushes you when standing and affects jumping) and the shortsword enemies that push you back absolutely moronic.
Oh and falling off is insta death instead of dmg and respawn. 

Quest design is stupid. 
I failed a quest because I took "the wrong route" when fetching an item for a questgiver because I chose the safer way around instead of going through screens of bull**** when it was never specified I had to take the direct way back. And now I'm locked out of the rest of that quest.

The Art and Lore are really good, but it's not worth looking past all the bad game design it's buried under.

If you are used to actually good metroidvanias/souls-likes  like Hollow Knight and Nine Sols, stay clear of this one.

I don't like this game.

The story doesn't make much sense, but that's not what I want to talk about. As a platformer souls-like, this game is punishing. In a way that [i]doesn't respect your time[/i].

Spikes and pits instantly kill you. The bosses lock you in a corner and force you to parry over and over again to survive a fight against a glorified health sponge. Platforming is clunky and unimaginative, and the mechanic of hitting an object to double-jump is terribly implemented. Most of the "magic" enemies don't make sense thematically and are extremely hard to hit - in a game where the main character is unresponsive and slow, these enemies are incredibly frustrating.

You'd think that the upgrades would help, but most of them are either gimmicks or lie about what they do. The moss in a jar SAYS it protects against poison, so you can survive in the sewer area, right? Wrong. Say goodbye to your entire fervour bar while trying to get items that could be helpful to progression. Or they might just be old body parts that some old fart seems obsessed with collecting.

It is also incredibly easy to fall through the floor.

The game is overall enjoyable but i have a few issues with it.

Firstly the hitboxes on enemys attacks can be bad with certain fights, in certain cenarios you'll be fighting an enemy and you want to jump over an attack (because there no dodge, which is fine in most cases) you think you'll clear the attack and wont get hit, but you still take damage even though the pixels of your character and their weapon dont overlap at all.

Secondly the dodge. Look i know i said that in most cases it would be fine but unfortunatlly this is not one of those cases. So one of the main ways you avoid stuff in this game is with a slide/dodge and i call it that because with certain attacks it works as a dodge passing right through them but with others you'll get hit regardless, again in most cases i would be able to look past this because you also have a parry, but with most enemys or bosses their attacks are un parryable which again would be fine if there was a consistent dodge but there isnt.
So in total the game is well made and the atmosphere is amazing but the combat feels like im gambling weather ill be able to dodge an attack or get hit, so decent but not good.
7/10

P.s. i could just be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ at the game and this is all my fault which is totally a possibility but that dosent really change how i feel about the game.

[strike] Souls-like [/strike] Chore-like gameplay coupled with painfully annoying, sluggish controls. Almost every single time you get hit you don't feel like it's your fault but its because of the ♥♥♥♥ hitboxes or the lack of mobility compared to your foes. The most dangerous obstacles are the regular enemies that are annoyingly placed. especially those ghost ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that become invulnerable after a single hit and then teleport somewhere else and shoot a HITSCAN LASER YOU CANT DODGE(also takes like 5 hits to kill hahaha so much fun). The bosses are trivial I think I killed all of them I've encountered so far in my first try. The parry mechanic is functionally useless because forget riposting you don't even get a chance to counterattack from most enemies attacks after a parry because they push you to the other side of the screen. The execution function is basically useless too, half the time they die before u even get the prompt and when you do, the animation takes so long and most of the time its not even that satisfying, and it gains you nothing so genuinely why bother with it? So you are just spamming dodge-attack at everything because that's the only viable strategy that doesn't take 10 years to kill all enemies. Half of the enemies can be dashed through the others cant and there doesn't seem to be an indicator which one is which so you just have to memorise it tough luck bucko.

Also how is this game almost 7 years old, has a sequel out and there is [b] still [/b] a known controller bug (every time you die your controller input stops being read and you have to press a button on your keyboard to respawn) that has not been fixed?!

will update this when I finish the game, if I can bear it. definitely don't see myself bothering to 100% it, or play the sequel tho. what a massive disappointment because the art style, theme and environment are so cool. I hope the movement opens up later on and it gets more fluid cuz man I dont know how much more of this I can take.

Blasphemous is a hauntingly beautiful and atmospheric action-platformer that expertly combines brutal Metroidvania exploration with challenging, souls-like combat. Set in the grim, religiously twisted land of Cvstodia, the game stands out with its stunningly detailed, grotesque pixel art and a deeply unsettling lore that creates a uniquely dark experience. Combat is deliberate, heavy, and unforgiving, rewarding precise parries and well-timed strikes with incredibly visceral and bloody execution animations. With its intricate world design, memorable boss fights, and an hauntingly melancholic soundtrack, it is a gripping and rewarding masterpiece for fans of dark fantasy and challenging gameplay.

By far, the best part of Blasphemous is the art, voice acting, and music. My favorite songs are the ones that played during the Crisanta and Isidora boss fights. Personally, the lore didn't grab me during my playthrough, but I hear it's quite good and there is plethora of resources online to explore it. The gameplay is fun for the most part, although both the combat and platforming are too basic for my liking, especially the latter. I very much enjoyed each boss fight, although only two of them were really challenging (mainly because of the stun-locking), those coincidentally having my favorite songs. Unfortunately, I would say a guide is needed as a lot of the quests are too obscure, and many of these quests have important relics/items needed for fully exploring areas. Overall, there's a lot of great and a lot of meh, but I still enjoyed the game.

collect items that are a mostly useless and learn the lore of pointless artifacts but the greatest enemy in this game is the clumsy attack and defense mechanics, - especially the attack animations that leave you vulnerable.

I understand making a game "retro" but there's no reason to ignore what makes games better now.

Movement is clunky and input lag makes fighting feel like a slog.

Enemy placement is like the original Castlevania, intenionally a** to pad gametime by making traversing unnecessarily hard. 

Hitboxes are inconsistent. 
There's no telegraphing of what enemies you can safely dash through and which will dmg you for trying. 
Parry is a thing that exists but it's completely random what enemies can actually be parried and which ones will push you back into the next abyss. 
Right at the start there's 2 types that use one-handed shortswords, one can be parried, the other pushes you back. 
Which makes the choice to make the first area right after Tutorial a Mountain with changing winds (pushes you when standing and affects jumping) and the shortsword enemies that push you back absolutely moronic.
Oh and falling off is insta death instead of dmg and respawn. 

Quest design is stupid. 
I failed a quest because I took "the wrong route" when fetching an item for a questgiver because I chose the safer way around instead of going through screens of bull**** when it was never specified I had to take the direct way back. And now I'm locked out of the rest of that quest.

The Art and Lore are really good, but it's not worth looking past all the bad game design it's buried under.

If you are used to actually good metroidvanias/souls-likes  like Hollow Knight and Nine Sols, stay clear of this one.

I first discovered this game around 2022 I believe, when I was interested in the Metroidvania side of the gaming sphere. I didn't really think of actually playing them, but I did enjoy seeing those 'no damage' runs every now and then. Eventually though, I got it on April of 2024 as my first ever Metroidvania (I REALLY thought Hollow Knight would be my first, but I have a habit of proving myself wrong a lot). 

Now, I can understand why there are complaints about, for example, the movement system, the sometimes janky hitboxes, and the very strict platforming at times (which I will admit is not this game's strong point). It's kind of the reason why I dropped it shortly before moving on to Hollow Knight, which I actually enjoyed a bit more. 

Now I don't know what came over me, but this year close to around summer break, I decided to retry the game again.

Holy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥. I repeat. Holy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥. 

It's like something clicked for me when I came back. Now all of a sudden, after exploring more of the game, I was spending hours and hours between intervals and sinking my time into the game. I want to talk about why I love this game as much as I can.

So please beware of spoilers and the yap session past this point.

I ADORE the boss fights. Once I got a hold of the mechanics, how to use prayers effectively, and learning patterns with every attempt (typical stuff for a Souls-like), I got a sense of chill and excitement every boss fight, which I definitely appreciate as I am writing this. The hitboxes, movement, and eventually platforming were, despite still being present, less noticeably bad as I got better at the game, which is good news for me. It made me feel like I am actually getting more skilled and it made me excited to play more, especially when I would get to fight another boss sooner.
My personal favorites are (in no specific ranking): [spoiler]Tres Angustias, Melquiades, Exposito, Quirce, and Crisanta.[/spoiler]

The OST and Map Areas …

Better the second playthrough when you are already accustomed to the combat and mechanics. Controls can feel clunky, specially with a controller. Pretty frustrating sometimes (Miriam...). Aside from that, awesome art and music. Great story if you put some attention.

[h1]This game is [b]not nearly enough fun[/b] for the [b]frustrating tedium[/b] it asks you to go through.[/h1]
[b]Pros:[/b]
+ The animations are very smooth
+ The lore feels unique and original

[b]Cons:[/b]
- Movement and attacks are clunky making platforming [i]very[/i] annoying
- Default button assignment on the controller is completely irrational, and button reconfiguration doesn't get saved between sessions
- Button symbols and names are depicted in a nigh illegible font that replaces the common ABXY / 〇△☐✕ with unreadable numbers, making menu navigation utter guesswork
- Text scrolling doesn't work properly in the menu, which is annoying when an item's actual function is always hidden at the bottom of a wall of text
- Essential mechanics like ladder jumping, lantern bouncing and dash-slash are weirdly unreliable
- Customary Metroidvania mechanics like airdash and doublejump don't exist
- Hitboxes/hurtboxes feel unreliable due to misleading details in the sprites
- 99% of all upgrades to moveset and abilities don't make noticeable differences, causing item rewards to feel unsatisfying
- The 1% of useful upgrades are hidden behind extremely obscure puzzles
- You can lock yourself out of the DLC (and thus multiple endings) by 1. missing a hidden door that has no indicators for its existence, and then 2. accidentally beating the midgame roadblock boss before reaching the area that loops back to the other side of the hidden door through natural progression
- Ugly designs: Almost every NPC (friendly and enemy) is a lumpy naked person with disgusting disfigurements
- Sprite style and background style feel out of sync - the BG's planar coloring style feels more like the Wand of Gamelon BGs
- Enemy death animations are surprisingly gory and cruel, feeling a little too malicious for my taste
- The worldbuilding uses jargon that has a different meaning in the game's context to needlessly obfuscate the plot

I know the last 4 minus points are subjective, and I know that …

The game would be great if it was held by it's fantastic artstyle, musioc and narrative, but combat is a bit weak (very repetitive in options when you've played for hours) and it's more glaring flaw: the abysmal platforming.

Blasphemous' platforming is one of the worst i've ever seen in my life, from how clunky and annoyingly precise it is, how buggy the platforms are sometimes, how unforgiving it is despite it being so finicky. The mechanics are also all over the place: can hold onto a wall and press up-right to get ready for a jump, but try that with a ladder and you release it; the lamp-jump was a braindead idea, as you gotta attack-dash in the air but not press up, but if there's a ladder right after it you gotta make sure not to attack too much because even if you press jump in time, the character wont grab onto the ladder. So there's sections of the game where you gotta perform this weird up-right-dash-attack-release dash dont attack-up combo just to hop on a lamp and grab a ladder. Not to mention that you may want to grab onto a wall and climb up, so you go right-up-jump-attack.. works fine, but if you try on the left, it wont attack, you gotta time your release.

So, to sumarize: poor platforming mechanics that feel more like like performing a fatality rather than real platforming, buggy platforms, unforgiving deaths on failure that combined with the crap mechanics means you will waste a lot of time redoing stuff.

As is I cannot recommend it

Story and themes are actually life changing. However the game is actually insanely easy and the only thing that makes it "difficult" are the cancerous controls. Half of the time your inputs go through at random intervals. I'm literally going through the same exact parkour area doing the exact same inputs and it somehow comes out different literally every single time. Its like the game has a some sort of weird sub tick rate for dome reason. Most bosses just spam abilities until you realize you need to just tank up and face tank it and then kill them anyway because you don't actually need to dodge anything because its not worth the effort of fighting the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ controls anyway. I'm tired of games where instead of having to use quick reactions and strategy to beat bosses and levels you have to instead be fighting against the terrible clunky and random moveset and controls.

This game’s been in my sights for so long that it almost felt like I already knew what I was going to get, it was just a matter of experiencing it. Nothing in this game shocked or surprised me, but I still enjoyed the overall experience. Yeah, this is a very weird game, and like most metroidvanias is very obscure, but Blasphemous take this to another level, to the point that I couldn’t understand one tiny thing about the world. My fault too.

The first thing to adapt once I started was the slow and deliberate movement. Honestly, I don’t mind it. Sure, in some platforming sections this movement was really annoying, and I could use more mobility overall, something I heard the second game improves, but I adapted to how this game works. It’s pretty clear that is all very intentional and it doesn’t really affect the experience once you’re used to it. And I like how brutal the combat is, especially on sound, it can be very satisfying once you hit those strikes and finally finish the enemy. This adds to the atmosphere, which is the best thing about this game, combined with a killer soundtrack, everything is moody and the vibes are great.

As a Soulslike, the combat is more about timing and reading the enemy than combos and synergy with abilities, but the options we can have to aid attack can help. The beads are impactful, the upgrades on the sword too, and the special abilities make a huge difference, and that’s pretty much all I could ask for. Some of my unlocks on the sword I barely use, which I think is more on the game than me, feeling that there was no better option during combat, especially boss fights, than to just use my 3 (or 4) hit combo, with occasionally the down or up attack. Parry is a mixed bag. On one hand the timing is very forgiving, on the other hand it feels you get punished by parrying, especially boss fights, usually sending you very far away from the boss. There could be a balance there for sure, a tighter timing and more reward for hitting it. A…

This is actually a really well made 2D souls game which surprised me with its depth, polish and mechanics. The pixel art choice goes very well with the world this game offers and music is impressive too. There are some stunning set pieces as backgrounds and the NPCs are definitely inspired by weird medieval art. Took me 20 hours for my first blind playthrough and I managed to get the absolute worst ending possible XD, goes to show what a good souls-like this game is with respect to the lore. Don't ask me about the story, hear it from me, "The ways of the Miracle are twisted and mysterious".

No crashes, no lag runs very smoothly. 

There are some challenging bosses and platforming in this game too, but nowhere near Hollow Knight in difficulty. There's NG+ which is where I need to try to find the best ending. There is also a boss rush mode, so there is a lot of replayability and game's worth here. For the price point during sales, this is an absolute steal. Definitely recommended! --Sorrowful be the heart, Penitent One--

This game is basically religious horror turned into a Metroidvania, and somehow it works really well. The art, music, and overall atmosphere are probably the best parts. Everything looks disgusting and twisted in every aspect of the game.

Combat took me a while to get comfortable with, and the map had me wandering around like an idiot more than once. Still, once getting hang of it, I had a hard time putting it down.

Not an easy game, and definitely not for everyone, but if you like dark Metroidvanias with creepy lore and a lot of suffering, give it a shot.

[b][h2] Pros: [/h2][/b]
Beautiful pixel art and a seriously messed-up world.
Combat feels weighty and satisfying once you get the hang of it.
Great soundtrack and atmosphere.
Lots of secrets and weird little things to discover.

[b][h2] Cons: [/h2][/b]
Some bosses are much harder than they need to be.
The map can be confusing as hell.
A few platforming sections feel a bit awkward.
Art style and music are beautiful. Gameplay is definitely a standout in the crowded collection of modern metroidvanias. Def recommend.

the ambience of this game, the world it creates is a 10.
